title: The Dangerous Truth About Chiropractic Pseudoscience
description:
Can you cure all diseases just by twisting your spine or neck? That’s what chiropractors want you to believe. This so-called “alternative medicine” was invented in the late 1800s by Daniel David Palmer, a Canadian-American grocer and magnetic healer who also opposed vaccines. His big idea came from accidentally slapping a janitor on the back — who then claimed his hearing improved. Out of this one anecdote, Palmer invented an entire medical system.

Chiropractic is built on three false ideas:

Subluxation: That bones slip out of place and block nerves, causing nearly all diseases.
Nerve Impairment: That pressing or “adjusting” your spine restores health.
Innate Vital Force: A mystical energy, like “prana” or “chi,” that chiropractors claim to control.

None of these claims have ever been proven. Subluxations don’t appear on X-rays, spinal nerves don’t work like water pipes, and no “Innate” life force exists. Studies have repeatedly shown no clinical evidence that chiropractic adjustments treat any disease — except mild back pain, where results are no better than placebo.

Worse, chiropractic isn’t harmless. Neck manipulations can cause strokes, paralysis, broken bones, and even death. Cases like Laurie Mathiason, who died after repeated manipulations, show just how dangerous this quackery can be.

And yet, chiropractors market themselves as doctors, treat conditions they have no expertise in, and even discourage vaccines. On YouTube, “Dr.” Eric Berg pushes pseudoscience to millions. In India, only 14 clinics are registered, but more are popping up, preying on ignorance.

If you’ve searched for chiropractic pseudoscience, chiropractic fallacy, spinal manipulation risks, quack medicine exposed, or chiropractic debunked, this video gives you the rational perspective.

Like, comment, share, and hype this video so more people don’t get “manipulated” — literally.
